description: Home-turf context-bench task corpus (docs/plans/home-bench.md H1-1) — the mirror of testdata/contextbench/tasks.json's grep-native B1 corpus. Where B1 measured grep's home turf (governance/enforcement questions are absent by construction there — see B1's corpus-mix disclosure in docs/plans/falsifiability.md), this corpus measures fathom's: obligations, verify, blast-radius, claim-provenance, concern-scoped search, contradiction, and staleness. Every ground_truth here was independently hand-verified against the fathom repo's actual files at the commit noted in each task's `source` field (never derived from the live daemon's opinion alone, per the plan's fairness rule 1) — most tasks additionally cite what the live daemon's obligations/blast-radius/call-hierarchy tools returned during authoring, purely as reconnaissance, with the hand-verification recorded alongside. See `pre_registered_criterion` (H2-1), `post_recompile_rederivation` (mandatory pre-H3 step), and `unmeasurable_by_comparison` (the fairness-rule-3 capabilities deliberately excluded from scoring).

pre_registered_criterion.source_of_registration: docs/plans/home-bench.md design section (H2 pre-registration), committed in git before this corpus file's first results run — git history ordering IS the registration evidence, not this JSON block alone.
pre_registered_criterion.criterion: fathom wins home turf only if BOTH hold: (1) the fathom arm's success count across this corpus is STRICTLY GREATER than the grep arm's (equal-or-worse success = refuted, per the plan's design section); AND (2) the fathom arm's total tokens are <= 1x the grep arm's total tokens (no token premium for winning — unlike B1, which retracted at <5x reduction, home-turf's bar is tighter: even token PARITY is acceptable, a token premium is not).
pre_registered_criterion.verdict_recording: H3-1 (op-gated, docs/plans/home-bench.md) records the run's results artifact + verdict, honest either way, once run.
pre_registered_criterion.caveats_carried_from_b1: n=1 corpus, single machine, dollar-cost not pre-registered as a criterion (recorded for context only, per B1-3's precedent).

post_recompile_rederivation.rule: H3's own gate mandates the operator recompile fires BEFORE the run — which re-cites obligations claims fresh at their new source lines and may re-scope rules. Every task listed below has a premise or ground truth pinned to the PRE-recompile store (compile watermark 538b9a8, 2026-07-08): before H3 fires, re-derive each exposed task against the post-recompile daemon AND re-hand-verify it against the repo at the run commit, updating prompt premises and ground truths in a committed corpus revision. H1-T12 in particular INVERTS: its 'verdict: stale' claim will be re-cited fresh by the recompile — re-anchor T12 to a claim that is drifted at run time, or, if the post-recompile sweep shows zero drifted claims, move T12 to unmeasurable_by_comparison for that run and score the remaining 12 tasks. Re-derivation updates premises and ground truths ONLY — the pre-registered criterion above is never touched by this step.
post_recompile_rederivation.note: H1-T08 was recompile-exposed in its original form (it asked which rule the compiler scoped uniquely to a file — a compile-time LLM decision); its critic-round rework re-anchored it to on-disk CLAUDE.md text, removing the exposure.

Hand-verified directly: CLAUDE.md's dogfood item 2 ('Refresh through the server, never the CLI') reads 'The daemon holds the / single-writer DuckDB lock, so a shell `fathom ingest` fails with a lock / error.' — directly contradicts the proposed 'always safe... even while the daemon is running' addition. This is a constructed synthetic diff (per the plan's design section), scored against real, already-committed text rather than a store mutation: fathom's contradiction_scan tool operates over ingested symbol observations with differing kind/claim (internal/query/engine.go:447 detectContradictions), not prose-level doc contradictions, so no fathom tool call is expected to out-perform a careful read here — recorded honestly as a task where both arms have equal structural access (see unmeasurable_by_comparison for the genuinely index-only contradiction capability this task deliberately does NOT test).
tasks.notes: Scoring changed to any-of in the critic round (D4): the prompt asks for 'the key conflicting phrase' (singular), so a correct answer quoting only one of the two phrases must pass — all-of would have failed correct single-quote answers.

tasks.notes: RECOMPILE-EXPOSED (critic D1 — the corpus's sharpest case): this verdict INVERTS after the operator recompile H3 itself mandates (the claim gets re-cited fresh at the new line). unmeasurable_by_comparison.capability: Compiled claim status (fresh/stale/contradicted/superseded) for an ARBITRARY file+rule, given ONLY the file path — no historical citation supplied in the prompt.
unmeasurable_by_comparison.why_grep_has_no_path: The ORIGINAL cited line range at compile time (e.g. CLAUDE.md#L140-L141 for H1-T12) exists only inside semantic_claims — nowhere on disk, not in git history, not reconstructable by reading current files. H1-T12/H1-T13 above are only fair because the prompt itself supplies the historical citation (extracted by this corpus's author via read-only reconnaissance against the daemon, then hand-verified); a task that asked 'is claim X currently stale' with no citation given would be answerable by fathom in one call and by grep never, at any diligence level.

unmeasurable_by_comparison.capability: Real compile economics: exact USD cost / token usage of the layer's last compile run (compile_runs ledger).
unmeasurable_by_comparison.why_grep_has_no_path: staleness_report's `layers._last_compile` block reported cost_usd: 0.047157 for the obligations layer's 2026-07-08 run — this number is written only to the store's compile_runs table (internal/store's PutClaims path via RecordCompileRun), never to any git-tracked file. No grep, however thorough, can recover it.

unmeasurable_by_comparison.capability: Claim feedback / refutation history (claim_events: who refuted or corroborated a claim, and when).
unmeasurable_by_comparison.why_grep_has_no_path: docs/vision/11-dial-to-eleven.md §1 (verified directly against the live fleet store during this corpus's authoring) records claim_events has ZERO rows fleet-wide — not just hard for grep, currently EMPTY for every claim, so no task could even be constructed with a real answer yet. Named here as a standing gap, not a scored task.

unmeasurable_by_comparison.capability: Exhaustive contradiction scan across the full live index (every same-named symbol across ~5,000+ symbols, all packages) — as opposed to the two-source, prompt-scoped contradiction task (H1-T11) actually scored above.
unmeasurable_by_comparison.why_grep_has_no_path: fathom's contradiction_scan answers this in one concern-scoped call (e.g. concern="store" surfaced a real `New` collision between internal/fusion/pipeline.go and internal/query/engine.go, and concern="compile" surfaced a real `compile` collision between internal/extractor/tsengine/tsengine.go and internal/filter/filter.go — both found via read-only reconnaissance and hand-confirmed by direct grep for `func New(`/`func compile(` respectively during authoring). Grep COULD in principle enumerate every function name repo-wide and diff signatures pairwise, but at repo scale this is not a task any human or agent arm can complete inside a bench turn budget — a real path in theory, not in practice, so excluded from scoring rather than padding either arm's number.
